subject: Nanotechnology
title: DNA Origami as a Fabrication Tool
description: A quick, practical guide to DNA Origami as a Fabrication Tool.

hook.text: Fold a long DNA strand into any 2D or 3D shape you want — nature's code becomes a nanoscale blueprint.

buildup.text: Short 'staple' strands pin a long scaffold strand into predetermined shapes — triangles, boxes, smiley faces.

discovery.text: Each staple can carry a nanoparticle or protein — DNA origami positions components with sub-5 nm accuracy.

twist.text: DNA is fragile — salt concentration, pH, and temperature must stay in a narrow range or the structure unfolds.

climax.text: Researchers use DNA origami to build nano-rulers, drug delivery capsules, and plasmonic antennas.

punchline.text: Fold DNA like paper and it becomes a nano-scaffold.

quiz.question: How does DNA origami achieve precise nanoscale positioning?
options: An electric field aligns DNA strands on a surface
Short staple strands fold a scaffold strand into a programmed shape
DNA molecules are stretched between magnetic beads
